result.summary: Do not close the gate: R6-3 remains unresolved. No new product finding beyond the named residuals. Executions confirmed ordinary dream-lock exclusion, current-ledger rendering, unchanged step-19 bytes, one additional write, both cleanup/concurrent-sync residuals, and the corrected exit inventory including :740. Executed production run() with proposed in-memory wiring, renderer/ledger/lock/cleanup functions, writeFilePrivate, and supervisor completion/failLoud with mocked I/O. Read the scoped diff/logbooks and supporting source; no implementation branch, unit suite, lint or RED proofs reviewed. Inspected source citations resolve; alerts.js:200 begins the catch whose return is at :201.

findings.title: Machinery: operative prose still directs the rejected design
findings.body: The Context explicitly says step 19 is the ONLY filtered render and failures render again unfiltered. AC6c at :1019 still requires step-19 omission, and Implementation notes at :881-884 still promise recovery on every post-step-19 failure. These contradict the corrected Deliverables/Table A and can steer implementation or acceptance tests back to the rejected mechanism. R6-3 is therefore not genuinely fixed.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile Context, AC6c and the residual note with unfiltered step 19, one filtered call after workspace teardown under the lock, and no recovery. Correct the logbook's reconciliation claim.

findings.title: Machinery: the required RED set contradicts revised AC7
findings.body: Table C requires the step-19 mutant to redden AC7a/b/c. Executing that mutation against production run() left every AC7c early-exit path unchanged: none reaches step 19. Conversely, the mutant changes successful step-19 bytes, violating AC7d, which the required set omits. Because observed failures must equal the declared set, this contract can reject correctly implemented tests or encourage weakening them.
findings.recommendation: Re-derive mutation failure sets against the revised acceptance tests. Remove AC7c from this mutant's expected failures, include applicable step-19 byte assertions, and distinguish old-branch measurements from unmeasured new declarations.

next_steps: Resolve the two machinery findings before closing the design gate or re-dispatching implementation.
